duration_secs.description: Total wall-clock duration of the run, in seconds.

schema_version.description: Version of this document's schema. See [`SCHEMA_VERSION`].

signature.description:
Detached signature over the canonical form of this document.

Excluded from the bytes it signs; see [`canonical_json`].

system.description: The machine and toolchain this was measured on.

tool_version.description: Version of the tool that produced it.

workloads.description: One entry per workload, in execution order.

BuildProfile.description:
How the measuring binary itself was compiled.

Two runs built with different optimisation settings are not comparable, so the settings travel with the result.

debug_assertions.description: Whether debug assertions were enabled. If true, the numbers are junk.

target_cpu.description: `--target-cpu` if it was set, otherwise the compiler default.

target_features.description: Target features the compiler was allowed to use, e.g. `"neon"`.

Pass.description: One measurement pass at a fixed thread count.

iters_per_thread.description: Calibrated work units per thread per round.

window_too_short.description:
Set when rounds were too short for the clock to resolve well.

`default` is required alongside `skip_serializing_if`: without it the field is omitted when false and then rejected as missing on read, so every report the tool wrote would fail to parse.

RunSettings.description: Parameters the run was executed with.

samples.description: Measured rounds per workload per pass.

threads.description: Threads used for the multi-core pass.

ScalingReport.description: How well a workload used additional threads.

efficiency.description:
`speedup / threads`. 1.0 is perfect linear scaling.

Values above 1.0 are real and expected on `Partitioned` workloads, where splitting the working set gives each thread a slice that fits in a smaller, faster level of cache.

speedup.description: Multi-thread value divided by single-thread value, direction-corrected.

multi_core.description:
Multi-core score, across every core the machine has.

Excludes workloads marked [`crate::kernel::Scaling::SingleThreadOnly`], so it is not directly comparable to `single_core` on a per-workload basis — only machine to machine.

reference.description: Name of the reference these scores are relative to.

single_core.description: Single-core score. `REFERENCE_SCORE` means "matches the reference core".

ScoreComponent.description: One workload's contribution to a composite score.

measured.description: Measured value, in the workload's native unit.

Signature.description: A detached Ed25519 signature over a report's canonical form.

algorithm.description: Signature algorithm. Always `"ed25519"` in schema version 2.

public_key.description:
Standard-base64 public key, so a verifier needs nothing but this file.

This authenticates *integrity*, not *authority*: anyone can sign with their own key. It proves a result has not been edited since signing, and nothing more. Establishing that a given key is trustworthy is out of scope for the file format.

Stability.description:
How much run-to-run variation a result exhibited.

Thresholds are expressed on the coefficient of variation of the retained samples. They are deliberately strict: a CPU benchmark on an idle machine should comfortably reach `Stable`, and anything worse is a signal that the measurement environment — not the CPU — is what is being observed.

oneOf.description: CV below 1%. Differences of a few percent between runs are meaningful.
CV below 3%. Usable, but only trust differences larger than the spread.
CV below 10%. The machine was busy or thermally constrained.
CV at or above 10%. Do not draw conclusions from this run.

Summary.description:
Summary of a set of benchmark samples.

All fields are in the same unit as the input samples. `median` is the headline figure; the rest exist to qualify it.

ci95.description:
Half-width of the 95% confidence interval on the mean.

Uses a normal approximation (1.96·σ/√n), which is adequate at the sample counts this suite collects and errs slightly narrow below n≈10.

cv.description: Standard deviation as a fraction of the mean.

median.description: Median of retained samples. This is the value to quote.

n.description: Number of samples retained after outlier rejection.

outliers.description: Number of samples discarded as outliers.

stability.description: Verdict on whether this result is trustworthy.

stddev.description: Sample standard deviation (Bessel-corrected) of retained samples.

SystemInfo.description: Description of the machine and toolchain that produced a result.

build_profile.description: Optimisation settings the binary was built with.

cpu_model.description: Marketing name of the CPU, e.g. `"Apple M4 Pro"`.

cpu_vendor.description: Vendor string where the platform exposes one.

efficiency_cores.description: Efficiency cores on a heterogeneous CPU.

l1d_bytes.description: L1 data cache per core, in bytes.

l2_bytes.description: L2 cache, in bytes. Per-core or per-cluster depending on the design.

logical_cores.description: Logical processors, as the scheduler sees them.

performance_cores.description: Performance cores on a heterogeneous CPU.

rustc_version.description: Compiler version, captured at build time.

target.description: Target triple the binary was compiled for.

timer.description: Behaviour of the timing hardware on this machine.

TimerInfo.description: Measured characteristics of the clock used for timing.

cycle_hz.description: Frequency of that counter, in Hz.

cycle_source.description: Hardware source of the raw cycle counter.

overhead_ns.description: Cost of reading the measurement clock, in nanoseconds.

resolution_ns.description: Smallest interval the measurement clock can resolve, in nanoseconds.

Unit.description:
What a workload's reported number means.

Carrying the direction alongside the unit is what lets the scorer combine latency (lower is better) with throughput (higher is better) without any per-workload special-casing at the call site.

oneOf.description: Billions of floating-point operations per second.
Gibibytes per second (2^30 bytes), as STREAM has always reported.

WorkloadReport.description: One workload's results across both passes.

error.description: Why this workload produced no result, if it failed.

excluded_from_multi_core.description: Set when this workload is excluded from the multi-core score, with the reason. See [`Scaling::SingleThreadOnly`].

multi_thread.description: Multi-thread pass. Absent for single-thread-only workloads.

scaling.description: Speedup and efficiency, when both passes ran.

unit.description: Unit of every value in this entry.
